draft.title: The colonies before 1763
card: Before 1763, Britain ruled thirteen colonies along the Atlantic coast of North America. They were New England, the Middle colonies and the Southern colonies.
Each colony had a governor, usually appointed from Britain, and an elected assembly. The assembly was chosen by male property owners and made local laws and decided local taxes.
Britain was far away and busy with other matters, so it left most daily decisions to the colonies. This gave colonists years of practice at governing themselves.

The colonies grew wealthy by trading farm goods, timber, fish and tobacco across the Atlantic and with the Caribbean. Britain expected this trade to follow British rules, but it was not always strictly enforced.
draft.remember: Before 1763 the colonies ran their own local affairs through assemblies and prospered from trade.

a.q: Which feature of colonial government gave colonists experience in governing themselves before 1763?
opts: Elected assemblies that made local laws and set taxes
Seats for colonial members in the British Parliament
A single colonial government for all thirteen colonies
Governors chosen by colonists to replace royal rule
a.why: Assemblies were elected by voters in each colony and made local laws and taxes, so colonists practised self-government. Colonists did not sit in the British Parliament, and governors were usually appointed from Britain.
a.clue: Think about who made local laws and taxes in each colony.

b.q: Why were the colonies able to govern most local matters themselves before 1763?
opts: Britain was distant and left daily decisions to them
Britain had given the colonies legal independence
Colonists paid no taxes to any government at all
Britain had no governors in the colonies at all
b.why: Distance and Britain's other concerns meant colonial assemblies handled most local decisions. The colonies were not independent, and they still had governors and paid local taxes set by their assemblies.
b.clue: Think about how far the colonies were from Britain.

a.best: Elected assemblies that made local laws and set taxes

b.best: Britain was distant and left daily decisions to them

problems.detail: "They were New England, the Middle colonies and the Southern colonies" reads as if there were three colonies. These are regions that grouped the thirteen colonies. It should say the colonies were grouped into these three regions.
The clue "who made local laws and taxes" nearly restates the right option, "assemblies that made local laws and set taxes", so a student can match the words without knowing the idea.
The clue "how far the colonies were from Britain" points straight to the only option that mentions distance, which gives the answer away.

check.summary: The facts are sound, but the card wrongly implies the three regions were the colonies themselves. Both clues give away the right answer by echoing its wording.

a.q: Which feature of colonial government gave colonists experience in governing themselves before 1763?
opts: Elected assemblies that made local laws and set taxes
Governors appointed from Britain to run each colony
A single colonial government for all thirteen colonies
Governors chosen by colonists to replace royal rule
a.why: Each colony's assembly was elected by local voters and made local laws and taxes, so colonists practised self-government. Governors were usually appointed from Britain, not chosen by colonists, so they did not give colonists this experience.
a.clue: Which part of each colony's government did colonists themselves choose?

b.q: Why were the colonies able to govern most local matters themselves before 1763?
opts: Britain was distant and left daily decisions to them
Britain had granted the colonies legal independence
Colonists elected every governor in all the colonies
Britain had stopped trading with the colonies entirely
b.why: Britain was far away and busy with other matters, so colonial assemblies handled most daily decisions. The colonies were still ruled by Britain and were not independent, and most governors were appointed from Britain rather than elected.
b.clue: Consider what Britain did, or did not do, about daily colonial affairs.
